card: Bitcoin Core ignores the addrMe address field received from Tor and I2P peers during local address discovery. Adversarial privacy network peers cannot legitimately see a node's clearnet IP, but could feed it a routable IP that the node might self-advertise alongside its listening port. This leaks custom listening ports to privacy peers and allows correlating clearnet and privacy network identities. The vulnerability was reported by researchers and requires outbound connection to the adversary and non-default port usage.
changed_since_previous: Includes unit test coverage in net_tests.cpp verifying both inbound and outbound privacy network connections are ignored by GetLocalAddrForPeer.
evidence: PR description: 'this fixes a fingerprint which makes it possible to correlate clearnet and privacy network IPs but it requires some not so easy preconditions: 1. we need to choose this adversarial tor/i2p peer to make an outbound connection to from our addrman 2. we need to be using a unique enough port.'
PR description credits researchers Loupe and instagibbs for finding the fingerprint.
problem: Tor and I2P peers cannot see a connecting node's real IP address, yet an adversarial privacy peer can provide an arbitrary routable IP in addrMe. If accepted, the node may self-advertise that IP combined with its own listening port, creating a fingerprint that correlates clearnet and privacy network identities for nodes using non-default ports.

risk.why: A mistake in local address evaluation could degrade automatic discovery and advertisement of reachable listening addresses.

scope_notes: A small single-line check in net.cpp accompanied by unit tests in net_tests.cpp.
summary: Ignores the peer's observed local address (addrMe in version messages) when connected through a privacy network like Tor or I2P. The check is enforced in IsPeerAddrLocalGood so addresses reported by privacy network peers are never treated as valid local addresses for self-advertisement.
